title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury
title_zh: 梭状芽孢杆菌Δ毒素靶向CD9以驱动NEC和脑损伤
abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is the most devastating gastrointestinal emergency in preterm infants, frequently causing mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment1,2. Although the gut microbiota has been implicated in NEC pathogenesis3–5, the microbial factors driving NEC and the following brain pathology remain unclear. Here we identify Clostridium perfringens pathobionts containing Delta toxin in the gut microbiome of individuals with severe and fatal NEC. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood–brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify the tetraspanin CD9 as the host receptor for Delta toxin. Using systemic, myeloid-specific and intestinal-epithelial-specific Cd9-knockout mice, we show that systemic and myeloid Cd9 ablation protects mice against toxin-induced lethality, blood–brain barrier dysfunction and multiorgan injury, whereas epithelial Cd9 deletion shows partial protection, implicating macrophage targeting as a primary driver of C. perfringens CD9-dependent pathogenesis. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. These findings suggest that a subset of NEC is a specific-toxin-mediated disorder and validate the Delta toxin–CD9 axis as a therapeutic target for this subset. A subset of necrotizing enterocolitis in infants is mediated specifically by the Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin.
abstract_zh: 坏死性小肠结肠炎（NEC）是早产儿最为严重的胃肠道急症，常导致死亡和长期神经发育障碍1,2。虽然肠道微生物组已被牵涉于NEC的发病机制3–5，但驱动NEC及随后脑病变的微生物因素仍不明确。在此，我们在严重及致死性NEC患者的肠道微生物组中鉴别出含有Δ毒素的产气荚膜梭菌病原共生体。临床上，感染婴儿预后更差，包括异常的全身炎症、严重神经损伤和凝血病。我们建立了一种小鼠模型，其中Δ毒素阳性产气荚膜梭菌感染，或单独的Δ毒素暴露，均可复现NEC的临床特征，包括肠道坏死和急性脑损伤。从机制上看，Δ毒素优先靶向巨噬细胞，强力激活炎性小体信号和凋亡凋亡，触发快速的炎症级联反应，破坏血脑屏障完整性并驱动神经炎症。通过全基因组CRISPR筛选，我们鉴别出四跨膜蛋白CD9为Δ毒素的宿主受体。利用全身、髓系特异性和肠上皮特异性Cd9敲除小鼠，我们证明全身和髓系Cd9敲除可保护小鼠免受毒素诱导的死亡、血脑屏障功能障碍和多器官损伤，而上皮Cd9缺失可部分保护，提示巨噬细胞靶向是产气荚膜梭菌CD9依赖性发病机制的主要驱动因素。此外，一种中和Δ毒素的单克隆抗体可防止疾病进展。这些发现提示，NEC的一个子集是一种特定毒素介导的疾病，并验证了Δ毒素–CD9轴作为该子集的治疗靶点。婴儿坏死性小肠结肠炎的一个子群特异性地由梭状芽孢杆菌Δ毒素介导。
